title: JCP&L Rebates 2026: Clean Comfort Heat Pump, Water Heater, Appliances
desc: What JCP&L pays New Jersey homeowners in 2026: Clean Comfort heat pump rebates up to $10,000, $750 water heater, appliance and thermostat rebates, Whole Home rebates up to $7,500 and free weatherization.
lead: JCP&L serves much of central and shore New Jersey, including Ocean County towns such as Toms River. Its programs are run through an online store and a set of applications. The biggest is Clean Comfort, which pays up to $10,000 to replace gas, oil or propane heat with a heat pump. These are the 2026 figures from JCP&L's pages and its Clean Comfort application, read on October 6, 2026.
cards_intro: JCP&L says rebates are subject to available funds and can change or end without notice. Each card names the fact with the date and source link.

cards.title: Clean Comfort: replace gas, oil or propane heat
cards.note: Lesser of $10,000 or 50% of cost; moderate-income lesser of $12,000 or 60%. Up to $2,000 each for ducts and removal, $2,000 for each extra cold climate unit. Installed February 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

cards.title: Clean Comfort extras
cards.note: Heat pump water heater $750, induction cooking $400 ($600 moderate-income), heat pump dryer $400, panel upgrade $300 per 240-volt circuit or up to $4,000 for income-qualified homes.

cards.title: Standard heat pump
cards.note: Air source up to $1,000, ductless up to $750, ground source up to $1,500. Tier tables were not readable.

cards.title: Smart thermostat and furnace fan
cards.note: ENERGY STAR smart thermostat per unit, and a furnace fan with an efficient motor.

cards.title: Appliances and water heater
cards.note: Heat pump water heater $750, dryer up to $300, washer up to $150, refrigerator up to $100, dehumidifier $40, room air conditioner $30.

cards.title: Whole Home Energy Solutions
cards.note: $2,000 plus $200 for every point of modeled savings above 5%, up to 50% of cost, with 0% loans of $2,500 to $25,000.

cards.title: Income-qualified weatherization
cards.note: No-cost upgrades plus up to $2,500 in healthy home improvements.

sections: JCP&L serves Ocean County customers, including the Holiday City section of Toms River. It also serves counties such as Monmouth, Morris and Middlesex. Atlantic City Electric serves part of Ocean County too, so Toms River readers should check the name on the bill. If it says PSE&G, see the PSE&G page.

Clean Comfort is for existing single-family homes. New construction is not eligible. The old heating system must burn gas, oil or propane. The heat pump must be a cold climate model on the Northeast Energy Efficiency Partnerships list, sized for the whole heating load, with equipment chosen using the industry's standard calculations. The project needs permits and a decommissioning form when the old system is removed. After you apply, allow six to eight weeks, and expect a possible inspection before payment.

JCP&L runs its rebates through a store site where you create an account, pick a product and apply with a receipt. Applications are due within 120 days of purchase, and equipment must be bought and installed from January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027. Both the outdoor unit and indoor coil of a heat pump must be replaced as a matched set. JCP&L adds that applying for the same incentive with a gas company at the same time is prohibited, so ask about the gas side first.
We found no battery rebate or rooftop solar rebate on the JCP&L pages. State solar credits and net metering still apply to solar owners. The federal credits ended after 2025.
claim_heading: How to claim a JCP&L rebate
claim_steps: Confirm your electric bill says JCP&L.
For a heat pump, ask a licensed contractor to quote Clean Comfort and the standard rebate separately.
Buy and install within the program dates, with permits.
Have the contractor, or you, apply within 120 days with the paid invoice and the equipment details.
Call 855-449-3090 or visit energysaveNJ.com with questions.
guides: Heat pump water heaters in New Jersey
faq: How much does JCP&L pay for a heat pump?
Up to $1,000 for a standard air source heat pump, and up to $10,000 ($12,000 for moderate-income homes) under Clean Comfort to replace gas, oil or propane heat.
Is Clean Comfort for new homes?
No. It is for existing single-family homes. New construction is excluded.
Clean Comfort equipment must be bought and installed by June 30, 2027, and the standard rebates have the same date.
Yes. Income-qualified weatherization offers no-cost upgrades of up to $14,000 for moderate incomes.
How long until I am paid?
Clean Comfort says six to eight weeks after your file is complete. Standard rebates say up to 30 days.
